key_insight: A lightweight, inference-time Target-Agnostic Guidance (TAG) module can stabilize object-centric grounding in Vision–Language–Action policies, preventing plausible but off-target grasps by refining or re-ranking candidate object-centric predictions.
problem_solved: VLA policies often fail in cluttered scenes because they mis-ground which object instance to act on—producing plausible motions that land slightly off the intended object or on a distractor. TAG addresses these instance-level grounding failures without retraining the base policy.
method: Run the base VLA policy to produce candidate object-centric predictions or action trajectories.

Apply a target-agnostic guidance mechanism at inference that evaluates and refines/reranks candidates using object-centric consistency cues (visual context, spatial priors, and language-vision alignment) rather than relying on explicit target labels.
Select the refined highest-confidence candidate to execute, improving instance-level grounding while keeping the original policy unchanged.
impact: TAG improves robustness of language-conditioned robotic manipulation in cluttered, real-world scenes by reducing misgrasping on wrong instances, enabling safer and more reliable deployment of VLA models without costly retraining.
visual_elements: Before/after scene comparison: same cluttered table with policy grasping the wrong object (before) versus correct object after TAG (after).
Pipeline diagram: base VLA policy → candidate proposals → TAG module (scoring/refinement) → selected action.
Heatmap overlays or attention maps showing how TAG shifts focus from distractors to the intended instance.
Bar chart showing qualitative reduction in instance-level grounding failures (misgrasp rate) and improvement in success consistency across clutter levels.
paper_title: TAG: Target-Agnostic Guidance for Stable Object-Centric Inference in Vision-Language-Action Models
paper_authors: Jiaying Zhou, Zhihao Zhan, Ruifeng Zhai, Qinhan Lyu, Hao Liu
